Rationale  
? Repetition breeds familiarity. A high volume of superficially plausible posts overwhelms fact-checkers and social platforms.  
? [Advantages: low cost for domain registration, easy to scale posting via bots, plausible deniability because items appear user-generated]

2. Emotional Manipulation  
Scheme  
? Exploit fear, anger, or disgust to trigger impulsive reactions—shares, comments, or even violence.  

Implementation  
? Craft sensational headlines (“They’re Coming to Your Town!”) and pair with emotionally charged images or short videos  
? Target community-specific forums, WhatsApp or Telegram broadcast lists, and regionally focused Facebook groups

3. Scapegoating Narratives  
Scheme  
? Portray a particular ethnic, religious, or political group as the root of social or economic problems, justifying retaliation.

Functional Example

Rationale  
? Scapegoating rallies an in-group, reduces moral resistance to violence, and simplifies complex issues into a single villain.

2. Synthetic Identity Fraud  
   ? Scheme  
     – Fabricate entirely new “persons” by combining real data points (e.g. valid SSNs of minors or deceased persons) with invented names and addresses.  
   ? Implementation  
     – Assemble identities through data brokers (e.g. LexisNexis) or public records; add fake driver's-license scans created with document-forgery kits.

     – Synthetic identities are hard for victims to detect (no direct victim), credit bureaus take longer to flag them, and criminals can scale by spinning up dozens of profiles at once.

   ? Scheme

   ? Rationale  
     – Direct access to real accounts bypasses many AML controls; stolen session cookies avoid triggering password-reset alerts; quick cash-out through pre-established mule networks.
